sections.content: How many people are "other registered nursing professionals"?

394,800 people

were counted on the census as "other registered nursing professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the seventh most common occupation reported on the census.

Other registered nursing professionals provide general nursing care for the sick, injured and others in need of care, assist medical doctors with their tasks and work with other healthcare professionals in a variety of other professional nursing occupations not elsewhere classified.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "other registered nursing professionals" there were more women than men (87.8% compared with 12.2%).

This means "other registered nursing professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 12.2% and women made up 87.8% of "other registered nursing professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other registered nursing professionals" included:

  • registered specialist nurses
  • educational support assistants
  • playworkers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "other registered nursing professionals" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "other registered nursing professionals", 15% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other registered nursing professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other registered nursing professionals" included:

  • engineering project managers and project engineers
  • office supervisors
  • senior care workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "other registered nursing professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "other registered nursing professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other registered nursing professionals", 9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (73.4% compared with 26.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.9%) than self-employed (3.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
